glosses: if; if it's the case that
if you're talking about; as for
patterns.usage_note: Picks up something already in play, what the other person just said or a topic on the table, and answers it with advice, an offer, or a judgment (温泉なら平日がいい). It attaches straight to a bare noun (それなら), and commands, requests, and statements of intention are free in its main clause, which と bars outright. It also has no fixed time order: 日本へ行くなら地図を買っておきなさい puts the buying before the trip, where 行ったら puts it after.

examples.ruby: 駅前[えきまえ]のカフェなら、八時[はちじ]から開[あ]いているよ。
examples.english: If you mean the cafe by the station, it's open from eight.

examples.ruby: 温泉[おんせん]に行[い]くなら、平日[へいじつ]のほうが空[す]いている。
examples.english: If you're going to a hot spring, weekdays are less crowded.

examples.ruby: そんなに眠[ねむ]いなら、先[さき]に休[やす]んでいいよ。
examples.english: If you're that sleepy, go ahead and turn in first.

patterns.usage_note: Names an action the speaker treats as reckless and follows it with an exaggerated disaster, so the main clause is nearly always undesirable and the tone is dread or grumbling (文句を言おうもんなら三倍返しだ). It attaches to the volitional form, and 少しでも or 一度でも sharpens the "so much as" reading. The sibling 〜ものなら on a potential verb (戻れるものなら) expresses a wish rather than a threat; もんなら is the spoken contraction of ものなら in both.

examples.ruby: 部長[ぶちょう]に文句[もんく]を言[い]おうもんなら、三倍[さんばい]になって返[かえ]ってくる。
examples.english: Breathe one complaint to the boss and you'll get it back threefold.

examples.ruby: 一度[いちど]でも遅[おく]れようもんなら、二度[にど]と誘[さそ]ってもらえない。
examples.english: Show up late even once and you'll never be invited again.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]のプリンを食[た]べようもんなら、一日中[いちにちじゅう]口[くち]をきいてもらえない。
examples.english: Eat so much as my little brother's pudding and he won't speak to you all day.

glosses: if you can, then (go ahead and) …
patterns.usage_note: Names a condition the speaker regards as barely possible, and in practice almost always attaches to a potential verb (戻れる, できる, 止められる). Two settings dominate: a wistful wish, where the main clause ends in 〜たい, and a taunt, where it ends in 〜てみろ and dares the listener to try. The volitional-form sibling 〜(よ)うものなら predicts a disaster instead; もんなら is the casual contraction of ものなら.

examples.ruby: 学生時代[がくせいじだい]に戻[もど]れるもんなら戻[もど]りたい。
examples.english: If I could go back to my student days, I'd go in a heartbeat.

examples.ruby: できるものなら、この痛[いた]みを半分[はんぶん]引[ひ]き受[う]けたい。
examples.english: If it were only possible, I'd take half of this pain on myself.

examples.ruby: 追[お]いつけるもんなら、追[お]いついてみろよ。
examples.english: Catch up with me if you think you can.
